newsitem.title: UK: Higher NWE gas oil closes Asian arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Higher NWE gas oil closes Asian arbitrage.

text.p: Higher European gas oil prices closed the arbitrage to India, but heating oil demand in Germany was picking up slightly, and talk continued of a squeeze on the IPE, dealers said on Thursday.
IPE Nov gas oil futures jumped $3.75 to $218.75 per tonne, and the Nov/Dec IPE backwardation firmed by another $3.00 to $9.50.

Heating oil on the Rotterdam barge market was steady at between Nov -25 cents to +50 cents fob ARA. Heating oil cargoes were very thinly talked, but one trader reported a bid at up to Dec +$8.00 cif Hamburg for Nov 10-20 delivery.
Traders who had been watching an opening arbitrage to India saw it close again as European prices rose.

Some had even tried to move Russian from Ventspils to the east because the Mediterranean was tight on high sulphur grades after Turkey's latest tender. But the port was closed due to high winds on Wednesday night and no trade was reported.
EU diesel was steady but still depressed with some cargoes available and valued at just Dec +$15 cif NWE.
